::: {.home-content .justify}
I am a Postdoctoral Scholar at the [Department of Biology, University of Padova](https://www.biologia.unipd.it/), where I work at the intersection of computational pathology, bioinformatics, and multi-omics data integration. My research focuses on developing efficient and scalable statistical/computational methods for single-cell RNA-seq, spatial transcriptomics, and whole-slide histopathology image analysis.

In my work on digital pathology, I design and benchmark algorithms for whole-slide image analysis — including cell segmentation, feature extraction, and representation learning — using CNNs and foundation models to extract morphological and spatial features, and to integrate imaging with molecular data for cancer research.

This methodological work extends to the development of open-source [software](publications.qmd#software), where I build R/Bioconductor packages and reproducible workflows for omics and imaging data, with an emphasis on GPU-accelerated methods and R–Python interoperability.

I have also enjoyed teaching statistics, genomics, and bioinformatics to students at the University of Padova, and I'm actively involved in the Bioconductor community, including co-organizing the CSAMA summer school.
